page_title: CodeKit — THE Mac App for Web Developers

sources.entry: CodeKit - Web development tool for compiling and auto-refreshing.

summary.name: CodeKit
summary.one_liner: CodeKit is a fully native Mac app that bundles web development tools for compiling preprocessed languages, auto-refreshing and syncing browsers, optimizing assets, managing npm, and building projects.
use_cases: Compiling Sass, Less, or TypeScript to CSS and JavaScript
Auto-refreshing browsers while editing a site
Testing a page across multiple devices at once
Compressing images and minifying assets before deployment
Setting up Tailwind, Bootstrap, or Foundation projects
summary.what_it_does: CodeKit is a Mac app that compiles many front-end languages (including Sass, Less, Stylus, CoffeeScript, TypeScript, Pug, and Markdown) through a UI with per-tool options, without build scripts. It auto-refreshes and syncs browsers across devices, with CSS changes injected without a full page reload. It includes optimization tools for images, JavaScript, CSS and HTML, plus cache busting and source maps. It also provides an npm interface for installing and updating packages, project templates for Tailwind, Bootstrap and Foundation, a parallel build pipeline, and ESLint integration.
notable: Browser sync and refresh to Mac, iOS, Android, Windows devices with no plugins or certificates needed for TLS
AI agent control: any agent that can run terminal commands can drive the app
Compiles many languages via checkbox options and a UI, with support for adding custom file types
Built-in npm UI for installing over 1,300,000 packages
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page text provided
Page says 'Animations are coming', indicating unfinished features
Page text is largely marketing; claims such as 80% image size reduction are vendor statements
